points.requirement: A generic normal epithelial lining borders a lumen; an extracellular basement membrane lies outside basal surfaces and differs from the plasma membrane around each cell. It is not a universal breast blueprint or invasion test.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Epithelium forms linings, coverings and glands; an epithelial cell is not necessarily malignant. A basement membrane is extracellular supporting material beneath an epithelium, distinct from each cell’s lipid membrane. Stroma includes supporting cells, extracellular matrix and vascular structures, rather than only collagen or fibroblasts. Immune cells and other nonmalignant cells can contribute to a tumor specimen. The relevant compartments depend on the tissue and disease.
evidence.explanation: The generic lining and extracellular basement boundary are distinct from each lipid cell membrane. The fields keep tissue architecture and site-specific exceptions, preventing a universal breast or invasion rule from this schematic. Read depth: Complete actual abstracts or individually logged targeted official/review passages and two Dostie PDF pages; no whole primary-paper/protocol or wholesale baseline-claim verification. Construction boundary: Toy examples are hypothetical; colors, geometry, counts and arrows are schematic conventions, not biological frequencies or approval/clinical evidence.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: An epithelial marker helps identify a cell compartment; a positive lineage stain alone does not establish malignancy or invasion. Tissue architecture matters. For an epithelial carcinoma, assessing in-situ versus invasive disease includes microscopic review of the basement membrane and surrounding tissue. The SEER summary-stage manual retains site-specific exceptions; this boundary is not a universal staging rule for every cancer.

Origin, distribution, harmfulness and transmissibility are separate questions; neither a variant class nor a large read fraction settles them.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In two invented histories, an early constitutional variant may be inherited or de novo, whereas a later variant can mark a mosaic body-cell lineage, including a normal blood clone.
